descriptors.definition: Bodies established by the Central Government to pronounce binding determinations on tax questions for applicants under Chapter XIX-B. These boards consist of two officers not below the rank of Chief Commissioner.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Income-tax Authorities and Appellate Tribunals by specific statutory jurisdiction.

descriptors.concept_name: Constitution of Board for Advance Rulings
descriptors.definition: The Central Government may constitute one or more Boards for Advance Rulings by official notification. Every such Board comprises two members nominated by the Board who hold a rank not below Chief Commissioner.
inclusion: Constitution of multiple benches with designated headquarters
exclusion: Appointment of officers below Chief Commissioner rank
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general tax assessment machinery by specialized membership and administrative setup.

descriptors.concept_name: Definitions of Advance Ruling and Applicant
descriptors.definition: An advance ruling covers determinations for non-residents, specified resident transactions, tax computations, and avoidance arrangements. An applicant includes non-residents, residents meeting monetary thresholds, and notified public sector companies.
exclusion: General taxpayers not falling under specified categories
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between non-resident application rights and restricted resident eligibility criteria.

descriptors.definition: An eligible person may apply for an advance ruling in quadruplicate through electronic means accompanied by prescribed fees based on transaction value. Applicants retain the right to withdraw their application within a specific statutory window.
inclusion: Tiered fee structures based on transaction scale
exclusion: Applications submitted without proof of required fee payment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes filing procedures and sliding-scale fees from standard tax return filings.

descriptors.definition: Upon receiving an application, the Board consults the Commissioner, examines relevant records, and either allows or rejects the application. Valid applications must receive a pronounced ruling within six months after providing a hearing opportunity.
inclusion: Mandatory opportunity of being heard before rejection
Statutory six-month time limit for ruling pronouncement
exclusion: Rejection of applications without providing reasons
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes initial admissibility checks from the substantive evaluation of tax questions.

descriptors.concept_name: Void Advance Rulings and Board Powers
descriptors.definition: An advance ruling obtained through fraud or misrepresentation may be declared void ab initio by the Board. The Board possesses civil court powers for discovery, enforcing attendance, and examining witnesses under oath during judicial proceedings.
inclusion: Declarations of nullity due to factual misrepresentation
Civil court powers for evidence collection and inspection
exclusion: Civil court status for criminal procedure provisions affecting the administration of justice
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes administrative voiding due to fraud from normal appellate reversals.

descriptors.concept_name: Powers of the Board for Advance Rulings
descriptors.definition: The Board exercises specific powers equivalent to a civil court regarding evidence inspection, witness attendance, and document production. Proceedings before the Board are treated as judicial proceedings for statutory contempt and penal purposes.
inclusion: Compelling production of books of accounts
exclusion: Exemption from being categorized as a civil court under specific criminal procedure chapters
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes quasi-judicial evidence-gathering powers from regular executive tax collection functions.

descriptors.definition: An aggrieved applicant or an Assessing Officer directed by the Commissioner can appeal rulings to the High Court within a specified timeframe. The High Court may extend this filing period upon proving sufficient cause for delay.
inclusion: Sixty-day base window for filing appeals
Discretionary thirty-day extension for sufficient cause
exclusion: Direct appeals bypassing the High Court level
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes appellate judicial review by High Courts from initial board-level proceedings.
